claim: In an Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ cluster deployment, Amazon MQ automatically manages broker policies to enable classic mirroring across all nodes, and creates a default system policy that sets ha-mode to all and ha-sync-mode to automatic so data is replicated to all nodes across Availability Zones.
question: How does an Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ cluster replicate classic queues by default?

values.display: classic mirroring across all nodes
sets the ha-mode to all and ha-sync-mode to automatic

qualifiers.scope: Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ cluster deployment
qualifiers.condition: classic mirroring applies to RabbitMQ versions that support it

evidence.quote: In a cluster deployment, Amazon MQ automatically manages broker policies to enable classic mirroring across all nodes, ensuring high availability (HA). Each mirrored queue consists of one main node and one or more mirrors.

Amazon MQ creates a default system policy that sets the ha-mode to all and ha-sync-mode to automatic. This ensures that data is replicated to all nodes in the cluster across different Availability Zones for better durability.

note: d063; RabbitMQ 4 no longer supports classic queue mirroring (What's New 2025-11-20); see quorum queues
